original_question: Let Td,c denote the class of d-generated, torsion-free nilpotent groups having class c. It is known that Td,2-groups are self-similar for all d, that T2,3-groups are self-similar, and that there are T4,3-groups that are not self-similar(A. Berlatto, T. Santos, Preprint, 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.16947). Are there T3,3-groups that are not self-similar?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.42 in arXiv:1401.0300v41 (The Kourovka Notebook, No. 21), section 'New Problems (21st Issue, 2026)', page 167.
correct_elements: Your draft is already essentially an exact restatement of Problem 21.42: it uses the same notation T_{d,c}, gives the same three comparison facts (all T_{d,2}-groups are self-similar; all T_{2,3}-groups are self-similar; some T_{4,3}-groups are not self-similar), and asks the same existence question for T_{3,3}.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the nearby paper-definition of 'self-similar' should be included: a group is self-similar if it admits a faithful state-closed representation by automorphisms of a regular one-rooted m-tree for some positive integer m (Problem 21.41).
If the notation T_{d,c} is retained, it should be defined inside the question itself; otherwise, spell out that T_{3,3} means 3-generated torsion-free nilpotent groups of nilpotency class exactly 3.
For maximal precision, replace the shorthand 'T_{3,3}-groups' by the full class description or explicitly state that 'd-generated' means 'generated by d elements.'
refined_question: Let T_{d,c} denote the class of d-generated torsion-free nilpotent groups of nilpotency class c. A group is called self-similar if it admits a faithful state-closed representation by automorphisms of a regular one-rooted m-tree for some positive integer m. It is known that every group in T_{d,2} is self-similar, every group in T_{2,3} is self-similar, and that T_{4,3} contains groups that are not self-similar. Does T_{3,3} contain a group that is not self-similar?
justification: The draft matches the official target almost verbatim. In the current arXiv PDF for 1401.0300, the relevant statement is the open problem numbered 21.42, not a broader neighboring problem. The only nearby hidden assumption needed to make the question fully self-contained is the definition of 'self-similar', which is supplied immediately above in Problem 21.41 on the same page. No explicit equivalent reformulation is stated there, so the refined version only makes that local definition explicit and keeps the scope exactly at the existence of non-self-similar groups in T_{3,3}.
